claims.text: A machine-learning potential can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The machine-learning potential can be trained on ab initio calculations covering only a subset of the relevant compositions and temperatures.
The proposed method applies to both solid and fluid states of high-entropy systems.
The machine-learning potential can capture the complex interactions and correlations present in high-entropy systems.
The proposed potential can faithfully account for vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
Capturing these interactions and correlations permits accurate prediction of phase free energies and thermodynamic properties.
The proposed method can predict free energies without explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The proposed method will increase throughput relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
Its fidelity will be comparable to or slightly lower than that of explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The proposed applicability boundary is systems containing more than three principal elements.
The proposed temperature boundary is 0.5 to 1.5 times the phase-transition temperature.
Accuracy may depend on the quality and size of the training dataset and on the compositions and temperatures being evaluated.
Failure to reproduce phase free energies, entropy, and heat capacity within 10% of the explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD results would falsify the hypothesis.
